stem: When counseling a transplant candidate about long-term skin-cancer risk, which immunosuppression-related factor aligns with standard references?

options.text: Immunosuppression intensity never influences skin-cancer risk
Only the first week of immunosuppression affects malignancy risk
Lower immunosuppression always eliminates skin-cancer risk entirely

explanation.rationale_correct: Skin-cancer risk factors include duration and intensity of immunosuppression, along with cumulative sun exposure, skin type, age at transplant, and transplant type.

rationale_incorrect.B: Immunosuppression duration and intensity are specifically listed as risk factors.
rationale_incorrect.C: Risk reflects ongoing immunosuppression exposure over time rather than only the first week.
rationale_incorrect.D: Immunosuppression intensity contributes to risk rather than lower exposure eliminating risk entirely.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 6, Noninfectious Diseases → skin cancer → Risk factors → iv.

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 6 → skin cancer → Risk factors → iv. (duration and intensity of immunosuppression); PDF p. 280 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Immunosuppression-duration/intensity risk angle distinct from older-age item (cctc-2161) and Fitzpatrick skin-type item (cctc-2153); anchor verified on Cupples p. 280.

stem: During pretransplant evaluation teaching about skin malignancy risk, which treatment-history factor aligns with standard references?

options.text: History of biologic therapy and phototherapy
Biologic therapy and phototherapy history lower skin-cancer risk after transplant
Only pretransplant antibiotic use is cited as a skin-cancer risk factor
Treatment history never influences post-transplant skin-cancer risk

explanation.rationale_correct: Skin-cancer risk factors include history of biologic therapy and phototherapy, along with history of skin cancer, autoimmune conditions, and lymphoma or leukemia.

rationale_incorrect.B: Biologic therapy and phototherapy are listed as risk factors rather than lowering skin-cancer risk.
rationale_incorrect.C: Biologic therapy and phototherapy history is specifically cited among risk factors.
rationale_incorrect.D: Treatment history is among cited risk factors rather than having no influence.

stem: A liver transplant candidate asks what head-protection measure aligns with standard malignancy-prevention references. Which counseling point is correct?

options.text: Baseball caps with no brim are the only recommended head covering
Hats are discouraged because they block all vitamin D permanently
Head protection is never recommended for transplant candidates

explanation.rationale_correct: Sun precautions include wearing protective clothing such as broad-brimmed hats and long-sleeve shirts and pants, along with sunglasses, sun visors, and sunscreen with minimum SPF 50.

rationale_incorrect.B: Broad-brimmed hats are specifically recommended rather than brimless caps alone.
rationale_incorrect.C: Broad-brimmed hats are recommended sun precautions rather than being discouraged.
rationale_incorrect.D: Head protection is part of cancer-prevention teaching rather than being omitted.

stem: A coordinator is updating skin-cancer risk and sun-protection teaching. Evaluate the following statements:

elements.text: Duration and intensity of immunosuppression are cited skin-cancer risk factors.
History of biologic therapy and phototherapy is a cited risk factor.
Broad-brimmed hats are recommended sun precautions.
Immunosuppression intensity never influences skin-cancer risk after transplantation.

explanation.rationale_correct: Immunosuppression duration and intensity, biologic/phototherapy history, and broad-brimmed hats are supported. Statement IV is false because immunosuppression intensity is specifically listed as a skin-cancer risk factor.

rationale_incorrect.A: Statement III is also true—broad-brimmed hats are recommended protective clothing.
rationale_incorrect.C: Statement I is also true; statement IV is false.
rationale_incorrect.D: Statement IV is false because immunosuppression intensity contributes to skin-cancer risk.
